content.title: About
content.content: Fried fish (NS) is fish that has been cooked by deep‑frying in oil at high temperature. The product features a golden crust, a fragrant aroma, and tender meat inside. It is commonly used in fast‑food dishes, snacks, and as a standalone meal.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Frying intensifies the aroma and creates a crispy texture.
Fish with firm flesh such as cod, hake or sea bass are often chosen for frying.
The tradition of batter‑fried fish comes from European cuisine, while plain dry frying is popular in Russia.
Fried fish is frequently served with sauces: tartar, mayonnaise, soy sauce.
In some countries it is sold as street food – the classic fish‑and‑chips.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Fish provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Despite frying, some omega‑3s remain, supporting heart and vascular health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Fried fish contains vitamin B12, niacin and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It supplies selenium, iodine and phosphorus, which aid thyroid function and bone health.

items.title: Easy digestion
items.content: Thermal processing makes the protein more readily digestible.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Frying increases calories and saturated fat, which may be undesirable in excess.

items.title: Acrylamide formation
items.content: High‑temperature frying can produce acrylamide, a potential carcinogen.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: Certain fish species can contain mercury or cadmium; choose reputable suppliers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fried fish can be enjoyed on its own, served with potatoes, rice or vegetable sides. It pairs well with lemon, fresh herbs, and a variety of sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fried fish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze in a bag at –18 °C, where it retains quality for up to 2 months.
